title: Kill Process
summary: Given a rooted tree structure consisting of n processes, where each process has a unique ID (pid) and a parent process ID (ppid), and an integer representing the ID of a process to kill, return a list of process IDs that will be killed, including the specified process and all its descendants.
statement: Given a rooted tree structure consisting of n processes, where each process has a unique ID (pid) and a parent process ID (ppid), and an integer representing the ID of a process to kill, return a list of process IDs that will be killed, including the specified process and all its descendants.
constraints: ppid[i] is the parent of pid[i], with 0 for the root. Return every killed process ID in any order.
hints: Parent identifiers define child adjacency lists.
Once a process is reached, all of its children must be reached too.
Map parent to children, then BFS from kill and append each dequeued process.
The traversal visits exactly the rooted subtree of kill; input order of each child list makes output deterministic.

tests.explanation: Killing 5 also kills its child 10, so return 5 then 10.
The root and both direct children are terminated in breadth-first order.
